capabilities.evidence: 20 isolated override cycles in native stress delivering begin_run and end_run exactly once each, 280 begin_draw deliveries across 40 cycles, 120 refused frames each proved to skip BOTH draw and end_draw, and 20 subset cycles in which a Game declaring only BeginDraw received none of the other three hooks; docs/foundation-35-game-frame-hook-evidence.md for the measured CNA_GameFrameHooks ordering
capabilities.notes: Game.BeginRun, EndRun, BeginDraw and EndDraw are complete as base bodies and reachable as methods, and a consumer may now OVERRIDE any subset of them by declaring the matching exported method on the object they hand to NewGame. Each canonical CNA hook is installed if and only if that override exists, so a callback object written before this existed opts into nothing and the native frame position is untouched. GameCallbacks still has exactly five members, there is no registration API and no exported capability interface, and the base is never run automatically: calling game.BeginDraw() inside an override is the Go projection of base.BeginDraw() and runs it exactly where the source says, zero times or many. BeginDraw's Boolean stays a channel separate from its error, and a refused frame skips Draw and EndDraw exactly as DrawFrame does in the reference.

capabilities.evidence: 20 isolated timing cycles in native stress: 120 settings reaching a live native loop (six per cycle), 20 non-owner-goroutine refusals, 20 argument-boundary checks, and 20 games created with a configured non-default target step
capabilities.notes: Game.TargetElapsedTime, InactiveSleepTime, IsFixedTimeStep and IsMouseVisible project as a managed field read plus a setter that pushes to the native loop, because in the reference the managed loop reads those same fields every frame and in CNA-Go that loop is native. SuppressDraw and ResetElapsedTime do the same. All six canonical operations were already exported by the pinned artifact and had never been reached from Go; the cna_game_get_* counterparts are deliberately NOT bound, because the reference reads its own field and a second source of truth could disagree. The Game's configured values are what cna_game_create is handed, replacing the literals it used to pass. The two TimeSpan setters differ by one IL instruction and the difference is preserved: InactiveSleepTime accepts zero, TargetElapsedTime does not.

capabilities.capability: Game.Tick and Game.RunOneFrame, and the standalone native session
capabilities.evidence: 20 isolated frame-step cycles and 20 Run-adoption cycles in native stress: 80 Ticks, 40 RunOneFrames, exactly 20 initializations (one per session), 120 Update and 80 Draw deliveries, 20 suppress-draw proofs, 20 post-Exit proofs, 20 non-owner-goroutine refusals, 20 in-callback refusals, 60 session-lifetime checks, 20 disposal checks and 20 recreation checks
capabilities.notes: The historical blocker was that a native game existed only inside the blocking Run, so neither member had a reachable moment. That was CNA-Go's architecture rather than CNA's: cna_game_create and cna_game_destroy bracket the game and cna_game_run is a separate call, so Foundation 47 split the SESSION out of Run. The first Tick or RunOneFrame creates the session on the calling goroutine, which owns its OS thread for the session's whole life; Run adopts a session a frame step created rather than making a second one, because whoever created the native game destroys it; and Game.Dispose ends a standalone session, which is the one state the reference cannot have and CNA's one-game-per-process rule makes mandatory. Measured, not assumed: a Tick on a never-run game delivers Update and Draw and NO Initialize or LoadContent, exactly as the reference's Tick does. RunOneFrame initializes first, which the reference's does NOT -- an upstream difference recorded in the Foundation 47 evidence rather than hidden, and not workable around, because CNA offers no route that runs a host frame without initializing.

capabilities.evidence: 100 isolated deliveries each of Exiting and the native disposal signal and 80 of Activated in native stress, in order and on the owner goroutine, across 80 runs including 20 second-run cycles on one Game; plus 80 managed Disposed raises across 40 dispose-after-run cycles and a measured zero raised from any run
capabilities.notes: Game.Activated, Game.Exiting and Game.Deactivated are bound to the pre-existing canonical CNA signals through cna_game_subscribe, because the reference raises all three from GameHost and the native runtime plays GameHost's part. Game.Disposed is NOT: the reference raises it from managed Dispose(bool) and from nowhere else, so Foundation 39 moved it there and CNA_GAME_EVENT_DISPOSED became a LIFECYCLE_ONLY signal that is still bound, delivered and counted -- it is what proves a registration outlives cna_game_destroy -- and raises nothing public. Exactly one native subscription per event per Game; the registration handle never reaches the public API. A second Run on the same Game releases the first four registrations and installs four fresh ones, proved 20 times with zero crashes, use-after-free or double frees. Game.Deactivated is structurally bound and separately recorded: see game-activation-transitions.

capabilities.evidence: 40 dispose-after-run cycles in native stress, each raising Disposed exactly twice from two Dispose calls and zero times from the run itself; behavior corpus and the external canary cover the component loop, the snapshot, the failure path and Dispose(false)
capabilities.notes: Game.Dispose(), Dispose(bool) and Finalize are projected from the pinned IL. Dispose(bool) copies Components to an array, disposes every element declaring the projected IDisposable member, and raises Disposed with the Game and EventArgs.Empty. It is deliberately NOT idempotent, because the reference carries no disposed flag: a second call disposes again and raises again. It reaches no native code at all, so a consumer may dispose after Run returns and still get the full managed semantics with no native handle left. Two reference steps are not reproduced and both are already-recorded deferrals: the graphicsDeviceManager disposal, whose field CNA-Go never assigns, and UnhookDeviceEvents, whose guard is the field HookDeviceEvents assigns and which base Initialize defers.

capabilities.evidence: 12 in-package tests, 6 Graphics-package tests that run the REAL cross-package bridge end to end, 6 behavior-corpus observations, and 3 external-canary tests from a module that imports both packages exactly as a consumer must
capabilities.notes: DrawableGameComponent is COMPLETE: 18 declared members plus 12 inherited from GameComponent, 30 Go identities, and it is the profile's first projected XNA-to-XNA derived type (XNA_COMPOSED_DERIVED_TYPES_PROJECTED 0 -> 1). The blocker was never the inheritance: Initialize resolves Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.IGraphicsDeviceService out of Game.Services, and the framework package cannot name that contract because the Graphics package imports it. internal/servicebridge resolves it with two function values installed from package inits -- no public API, no retained object, no import cycle, and no reflection at the call site. A program that never imports the Graphics package installs no resolver and resolves nothing, which is correct by construction rather than a gap: registering the service requires naming it. The type reaches no native code at all and is classified pure managed on that evidence; the device it hands back is native, obtaining it is not. It is also the profile's one SHIPPED IDrawable -- before this, every live IDrawable in a CNA-Go program was a consumer's own type.

capabilities.evidence: 20 isolated window cycles in native stress: 60 identity checks (three per cycle, before, during and after a run), 120 guarded-fallback checks, 80 unguarded-failure checks, 120 live reads against a real native window, 20 title-suppression proofs and 20 non-owner-goroutine refusals; plus 5 external-canary tests from a module that cannot see internal/interop
capabilities.notes: GameWindow is COMPLETE: 20 XNA members, 25 Go identities. Game.Window returns one stable identity for the Game's whole life, because Game::.ctor calls EnsureHost() and Game::get_Window is two field reads over what it assigned. Nine CNA window routes are bound; three canonical ones deliberately are NOT. cna_game_window_copy_title is unbound because GameWindow::get_Title is one ldfld over the abstract base's own field, and cna_game_window_get_current_orientation is unbound because WindowsGameWindow::get_CurrentOrientation is `ldc.i4.0; ret` -- a constant, not a platform query. SetSupportedOrientations was the one open question and the answer is that WindowsGameWindow's body is a single `ret`: the member does nothing, CNA's only orientation setter belongs to GraphicsDeviceManager rather than to the window, and forwarding to it would invent behaviour the reference does not have. Every other member follows the reference's own null-guard split: five answer a documented fallback with no native window and four report the NullReferenceException the unguarded ones produce.

capabilities.capability: GameWindow client-size, orientation and screen-device signals
capabilities.evidence: three native subscriptions installed and released per run, proved by the same lifetime path the four game signals use; zero deliveries measured under HEADLESS
capabilities.notes: The three canonical CNA window signals are bound through cna_game_window_subscribe, delivered on a trampoline table of their own -- the window and game identity spaces both number from zero, so one shared entry point could route a signal into the wrong projected event -- and released with the game. The HEADLESS artifact has no window manager, so it never resizes, rotates or changes screen and all three counters stay at zero. The raise paths, the routing and the handler-failure contract are proved without a delivery; an actual native delivery is NOT_RUN_ENVIRONMENT and is not claimed.

capabilities.notes: Borrowed from the Game-owned GraphicsDeviceManager; never synthetic. Game.GraphicsDevice is projected as graphics.GameGraphicsDevice by the cross-package cycle rule and reproduces the reference body exactly: it resolves IGraphicsDeviceService out of Game.Services and reports the reference's InvalidOperationException when none is registered. CNA-Go publishes no such service -- GraphicsDeviceManager satisfies neither service contract -- so a device comes from a consumer's own registration or not at all.

capabilities.evidence: the qualified artifact opens a real SDL3 playback device: a direct C probe against it reported is_playback_available=1, created a 22,050-sample PCM16 mono effect, measured its duration as exactly 5,000,000 ticks (0.5s at 44.1kHz), created an instance, played it and read back CNA_SOUND_STATE_PLAYING with volume 1.0
capabilities.notes: Foundation 1 recorded this as BACKEND_BLOCKED because its artifact was built with the NULL audio backend. That is no longer true and the classification was retired rather than restated: the current artifact is CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM=SDL3 and playback measurably works in this environment. The only remaining blocker is CNA-Go's own surface -- SoundEffect, SoundEffectInstance and the rest of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Audio are missing, and CNA-Go binds no cna_sound_effect_* route. AudioListener and AudioEmitter exist as pure managed descriptors and claim no runtime capability.
